introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

Figure 2 shows a transformer that a student intends to use to operate a small radio set.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

*Figure 2*

figures.legende: Transformer with a primary coil of 4000 turns on a 240 V a.c. input and a secondary coil of 250 turns feeding a 6 ohm resistor; output voltage V0.

incertitudes: Page de garde : la valeur imprimée de l'accélération de la pesanteur est « g = 10 m s^-5 » ; c'est une coquille évidente (unité m s^-2), retenue ainsi dans l'introduction et dans tous les calculs (g = 10 m s^-2).
Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : les totaux (`points` de l'exercice) sont la somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc.

Question 3 : le sujet donne 4000 spires au primaire (240 V a.c.) et 250 spires au secondaire, avec la résistance de 6 ohms en série sur le circuit de sortie ; lecture retenue de la figure 2. Le transformateur est supposé idéal.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the information on the diagram, calculate:

(i) the output voltage, $V_0$. *[2 marks]*

(ii) the current through the $6\,\Omega$ resistor. *[2 marks]*

(iii) explain whether or not the transformer will function normally if the alternating current in the primary circuit is replaced with a direct current. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The primary coil has $N_p = 4000$ turns with $V_p = 240\,\mathrm{V}$ a.c.; the secondary coil has $N_s = 250$ turns, connected to the $6\,\Omega$ resistor.

(i) $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$, so $V_0 = 240\times\dfrac{250}{4000} = 15\,\mathrm{V}$.

**$V_0 = 15\,\mathrm{V}$.** (It is a step-down transformer.)

(ii) The $6\,\Omega$ resistor is across the output, so $I = \dfrac{V_0}{R} = \dfrac{15}{6} = 2.5\,\mathrm{A}$.

**The current is $2.5\,\mathrm{A}$.**

(iii) **No, it will not function normally.** A transformer works by electromagnetic induction, which needs a *changing* magnetic flux in the core. A direct current produces a steady magnetic field, so the flux linked with the secondary coil does not change, no e.m.f. is induced and the output voltage is zero (the radio would not work). In addition, the primary coil would carry a large steady current limited only by its small resistance and could overheat.
